subtype: Approach: choosing the right moment and mood [Thinking]
passage: Emeka had the question ready at four o'clock: could he sleep over at Tobi's on Saturday? But Dad had just walked in with his shoulders low, phone pressed to his ear, talking about invoices. Not now, Emeka thought. Dad says yes when he is easy, not when he is tired. So Emeka did his reading, set the table and dried the plates. After dinner Dad leaned back with his tea and started the crossword. That was the moment. "Dad, have you got time for a small question?" Emeka asked. Dad looked up, smiling. "Go on." It was not yes yet, but it was "Tell me about it", and that was a start.

qa.q: What was Dad doing when Emeka asked his question?
qa.a: Dad was leaning back with his tea, starting the crossword.

qa.q: What was Emeka thinking about Dad's mood at four o'clock?
qa.a: He thought Dad was too tired and busy to say yes, because Dad says yes when he is easy and not when he is tired, so Emeka decided to wait.

qa.q: What else could Emeka prepare so the request goes well?
qa.a: He could have the details ready, such as where Tobi lives and when he will be home, since Dad is likely to ask about them.

qa.q: How might Dad have felt if Emeka had asked during the phone call?
qa.a: Probably irritated and distracted, since Dad was tired and busy, and he might have said no just to end the interruption.

grounding: A boy waits until his father is relaxed after dinner before asking about a sleepover.
